# GitHub profile README design study

Reviewed 30 individual profile READMEs on November 21, 2026. The sample includes popular profile repositories, independently discovered analytics and AI practitioners, and several visually expressive designs. Treat repository stars as an interest signal and the design assessments below as editorial judgments. Mobile and load observations for the references are inferred from their layouts and dependencies. The finished design was tested separately in a browser.

Discovery started with [Awesome GitHub Profile README](https://github.com/abhisheknaiidu/awesome-github-profile-readme), [Creative Profile README](https://github.com/coderjojo/creative-profile-readme), and the [Awesome GitHub Profile Gallery](https://github.com/nitr0yukkuri/awesome-github-profile-gallery). High-star anchors included codeSTACKr (~1.2k), Andrew6rant (~1k), DenverCoder1 (~748), sindresorhus (~504), abhisheknaiidu (~452), and simonw (~448) as displayed by GitHub during the review. Swyx also identifies himself as a GitHub Star in his profile. That recognition is separate from the README design.

## The 30 profiles

Each entry considers visual appeal and hierarchy, the header, motion, typography and palette, contributions or statistics, stack, project presentation, narrow-screen behavior, and delivery dependencies.

| Profile | Hierarchy and header | Visual system and motion | Activity and statistics | Stack and project presentation | Mobile and reliability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [simonw](https://github.com/simonw/simonw) | Current work first, then releases, writing, and TIL | Quiet GitHub typography, no banner or motion | Releases show real work in progress | Datasette and LLM above the feeds, no stack inventory | Text remains legible at narrow widths and useful between updates |
| [sindresorhus](https://github.com/sindresorhus/sindresorhus) | Brief personal line and two clear exits | Sparse GitHub text and a small unicorn motif, no animation | No stats card | Featured app and writing, no stack list | Minimal requests and comfortable wrapping |
| [antfu](https://github.com/antfu/antfu) | A single site-wide navigation strip | Minimal monospaced type, no hero illustration or motion | No stats card | Dedicated projects link, no inline stack | No widget requests, longer navigation wraps |
| [cassidoo](https://github.com/cassidoo/cassidoo) | Distinct greeting, personal intro, then projects | Conversational text and native GitHub colors, no animated header | No metrics | Direct links to apps and games, no stack wall | Plain text and lists scale easily |
| [mxstbr](https://github.com/mxstbr/mxstbr) | TL;DR résumé and selected essays | Native type, occasional emoji, no motion | Essay readership and update notes | Open-source work routed to a portfolio, no standalone stack | Single-column text survives stale essay updates |
| [swyxio](https://github.com/swyxio/swyxio) | Links and current AI work lead | Native type with a playful, interactive-looking endorsement list | Counts live behind issue links instead of a dashboard | Skills are linked individually, current projects appear in prose | Text is resilient, lengthy link list pushes content down |
| [abhisheknaiidu](https://github.com/abhisheknaiidu/abhisheknaiidu) | Contact leads into time tracking and personal telemetry | Native text, contrasting sponsor image and dark stats card | Weekly time, Todoist, and GitHub measurements | No strong project or stack index in the current README | Cards scale, outside services and stale telemetry can weaken the story |
| [Anmol-Baranwal](https://github.com/Anmol-Baranwal/Anmol-Baranwal) | Custom banner, bio, credibility, then writing and projects | Strong personality and colorful GitHub-hosted media | Contribution narrative and automated blog feed | Project descriptions explain what each tool does | Longer scroll, project text remains useful even if media fails |
| [DenverCoder1](https://github.com/DenverCoder1/DenverCoder1) | Branded nameplate over a clear set of sections | Pink monospace typing and consistent icon families | Streak card and recent activity list | Strong distinction between own projects and contributions, grouped tools | Dense tables and card text are more fragile on a phone, several image hosts |
| [anuraghazra](https://github.com/anuraghazra/anuraghazra) | Locally hosted illustrated header and compact bio | Playful art, concise icons, consistent widget theme | Profile and language stats alongside repository cards | A few inline tools followed by pinned project cards | Wide stats table can crowd narrow screens, cards rely on a public endpoint |
| [Platane](https://github.com/Platane/Platane) | One graphic carries the entire README | Animated contribution grid with light and dark assets | Contributions are the subject of the animation | No stack or project index outside the generator link | Fast to scan, small cells on phones, refresh depends on automation |
| [ryo-ma](https://github.com/ryo-ma/ryo-ma) | Trophy heading and a widget-led showcase | Game-like trophies provide visual continuity | Achievements dominate | The embedded demo markets the generator, little stack or project context | One scaled grid, hosted rendering is a dependency |
| [BrunnerLivio](https://github.com/BrunnerLivio/BrunnerLivio) | Website links above a live guestbook | Plain table and changing community content, no motion needed | Guestbook activity instead of contribution counts | Website is the main work link, no stack inventory | Longer cells can pinch on phones, updates rely on automation |
| [rasbt](https://github.com/rasbt/rasbt) | Name, research focus, and a compact list of links | Unadorned GitHub type, no motion or custom palette | No metrics | Specialties and books establish expertise, no stack list | Fast and readable at narrow widths |
| [karpathy](https://github.com/karpathy/karpathy) | One line of identity | Native type, no banner, motion, or color system | No widget | Neural nets establish focus, projects and tools sit elsewhere on GitHub | Immediate load and little mobile friction, sparse as a standalone introduction |
| [jeffheaton](https://github.com/jeffheaton/jeffheaton) | Short contact-led composition | Visual social links carry the identity, little supporting native text | No contribution dashboard in the prose | Platforms lead out to content, no inline stack or project catalogue | Compact, with higher dependence on image labels and destinations |
| [catalinmiron](https://github.com/catalinmiron/catalinmiron) | One product leads with a direct destination | Project branding and a real animation showcase video | No metrics panel | React Native expertise is demonstrated through a single product | Link remains useful independently of video support and media payload |
| [kattni](https://github.com/kattni/kattni) | Custom header, identity, and community work | Personal illustration gives the intro character, static media | Community and sponsorship stand in for stats | CircuitPython contribution is explained in prose, no logo wall | Single-column content and useful image alt text |
| [codeSTACKr](https://github.com/codeSTACKr/codeSTACKr) | Greeting, current work, tools, then content feeds | Social and tool icon strips, GitHub headings and rules | Recent contribution events and a stats section | Tools grouped, tutorials and course links carry the work | Icons can wrap, repeated feeds increase scrolling and maintenance |
| [Andrew6rant](https://github.com/Andrew6rant/Andrew6rant) | A custom dashboard acts as the full README | Strong terminal-style visual consistency, two SVG themes | Generated repository, language, and activity metrics | Project and tech information are secondary to the generated overview | One image response, with small image-only text at narrow widths |
| [pedrocatalao](https://github.com/pedrocatalao/pedrocatalao) | Four cards take the place of a bio | Native-looking cards show how a dense dashboard can feel coherent | Stats, languages, notable contributions, and streaks | Language totals substitute for stack and contributions substitute for a showcase | Generated SVGs avoid live widget API requests, small card labels can scale down |
| [rahuldkjain](https://github.com/rahuldkjain/rahuldkjain) | Name and focus first, then tools and posts | Standard GitHub type with emoji and icon-led sections | Blog refresh drives visible activity | Generator contribution call and a link to all projects, dedicated tools area | Text wraps well, image groups and feed jobs add dependencies |
| [kothariji](https://github.com/kothariji/kothariji) | Branded introduction, social links, then a visual footer | Badge-heavy art and an animated snake | Snake and service cards are the highlights | Front-end tools mentioned in prose, project cards take a back seat | Smaller images stack or wrap, outside widgets may render inconsistently |
| [lizheming](https://github.com/lizheming/lizheming) | Descriptive intro, contacts, talks, then stats | Emoji labels and native headings, motion plays little role in the hierarchy | Open-source work gets its own stats section | JavaScript, Node.js, and SVG named in text, talks link out | Prose remains useful if the last visual section fails |
| [MishManners](https://github.com/MishManners/MishManners) | Strong branded opening followed by community and content links | Expressive emoji, monospace Skyline, and a snake | Skyline artwork, stats, and contribution animation | Pins and channels show work, no prescriptive skills grid | Media and preformatted art are denser on phones, long page depends on several updates |
| [mazipan](https://github.com/mazipan/mazipan) | Role, experience, open source, then contact and support | Native headings and dividers with small social images | Community affiliations supply credibility | Frameworks in the intro, open-source communities are directly linked | Text-first structure is robust, media is mostly optional |
| [madushadhanushka](https://github.com/madushadhanushka/madushadhanushka) | Intro and visual tools strip precede curated and recent posts | Branded header imagery and familiar technology logos | GitHub statistics and top languages | Languages and tools are visible, articles do most of the showcasing | Many images and a long scroll, outside widgets can fail independently |
| [yoshi389111](https://github.com/yoshi389111/yoshi389111) | Project index organized by platform and language | Spare GitHub text and contribution artwork | 3D calendar doubles as a demo of the author's action | Descriptive project links grouped by GitHub Actions, VS Code, npm, and CLI | Lists read well on phones, calendar freshness depends on a job |
| [duonghuuphuc](https://github.com/duonghuuphuc/duonghuuphuc) | Research identity and a clear contact block | Native text with compact tool and social badges | No contribution widget carries the introduction | Programming badges and a linked AI project | Badge rows can wrap and the biography remains readable without images |
| [ashishps1](https://github.com/ashishps1/ashishps1) | Simple opening followed by learning resources | Native typography and restrained ornamentation | No activity card drives the composition | Learning repositories and videos carry the portfolio, no skills grid | Link-led structure is readable on narrow screens and easy to keep current |

## Patterns that carried into the design

| Approach | Strength | Tradeoff in this profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal developer profile | A short introduction and clear links work on any screen | Pure text leaves little visual identity |
| Dark dashboard | Themed cards make related information feel cohesive | Metrics and miniature chart labels compete with project explanations |
| Animated portfolio | Motion can demonstrate a process within one small asset | Looping copy and full-width GIFs command attention throughout the page |
| AI and data illustration | A pipeline diagram makes an abstract specialty concrete | Generic circuitry and unsourced charts would obscure what the projects do |
| Open-source maintainer profile | A named project, package link, and contributor path invite use and participation | A long release feed can push recruiters past the other work |
| Illustrated profile | A distinctive header adds character immediately | Decorative themes take up valuable space when unrelated to the work |

The design combines maintainer-first content with an illustrated data pipeline. A dark evergreen banner, mint accents, and one amber signal carry the same palette into the Oribi workflow diagram and stack icons. The README uses one column, with Oribi above two applied projects. The optional Instacart preview is an actual dashboard from Abdul's portfolio. The diagram and project copy retain their meaning at narrow widths, with essential details in selectable Markdown.

## Visual and activity choices

- **Animated header.** Animated typing is easy to customize and capsule banners supply quick gradients. Reusable GIF patterns, including developer loops and illustrated scenes, are expressive but need frame data and a separate still for motion-sensitive readers. A hand-drawn SVG lets the pipeline trace run once and respect reduced motion while the whole banner stays readable. [Readme Typing SVG](https://github.com/DenverCoder1/readme-typing-svg) · [Capsule Render](https://github.com/kyechan99/capsule-render) · [RyMe.md](https://github.com/ryanpolasky/ryme.md) · [An illustrated GIF implementation](https://christt105.github.io/blog/github-profile-readme/) · [SVG as an image](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Guides/SVG_as_an_image)
- **Activity.** The footer pairs a 31-day graph with a contribution streak card. Both use the banner's evergreen palette and update through hosted services. The link to GitHub's native activity provides a fallback. [Streak Stats](https://github.com/DenverCoder1/github-readme-streak-stats) · [Activity Graph](https://github.com/Ashutosh00710/github-readme-activity-graph)
- **Project media and tools.** Named logo tiles are grouped by use and wrap independently on narrow screens. Oribi's themes are handled within its local SVG, and the dashboard is a compact WebP. [Logo sources and licenses](assets/profile/tools/NOTICE.md) · [GitHub's Markdown formatting reference](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax)
- **Sources for the profile.** Oribi's public package and repository support its scope and installation. The portfolio source and public project READMEs support the internship affiliation and applied project descriptions. [Portfolio](https://samhoon.xyz/) · [Oribi on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/oribi/) · [Oribi on GitHub](https://github.com/samhoon000/Oribi) · [Instacart Customer Analytics](https://github.com/samhoon000/instacart-customer-analytics) · [Tamil Nadu Air Quality Analysis](https://github.com/samhoon000/tamilnadu-air-quality-analysis)

## Preview and verification

The screenshots show a local GitHub-style Markdown render. Chromium checks covered desktop and mobile in both themes, including 320 px wide, and a tablet layout. The checks covered horizontal overflow, image decoding, the dashboard disclosure, and the SVG with regular and reduced motion. The activity charts update through their hosted services. The previous Pacman workflow was removed.
